The airlock hissed open, revealing a cabin filled with gold-plated statues and silent, terrified eyes staring back from the dark. I reached for the emergency beacon, but my hand froze as I remembered the old man's warning: "Some debts are paid in silence, not in radio waves." Slowly, I turned my back on the living, letting the ship's dying lights fade into the endless void. Now I walk among the stars alone, guarding a secret that keeps the survivors safe from themselves.

prompt: When the cultists forced you into the room with the eldridge abomination, they assumed that you would instantly go mad as you tried to comprehend it. However, you are a grade A idiot and instead of trying to understand how it exists, you simply accept that it does, much to everyone' shock.
response: They dragged me into that dark room with the eldritch monster, screaming that my brain would melt trying to understand its impossible shape. I just looked at the writhing nightmare and shrugged, thinking it looked like a very complicated kind of spaghetti. "Eh, whatever," I muttered, completely ignoring the fact that the very air around it was turning into green slime. The cultists stared in absolute horror, expecting me to scream or faint, but I just asked if they had any extra sauce. They finally gave up, realizing that a grade-A idiot like me was the only thing standing between them and total madness.

prompt: Massive alien ships came down from the sky, guns blazing... but totally ignoring us. Instead, they attacked the trees and forests. If that weren't strange enough, the tree started fighting back.
response: Mamma mia, those iron monsters from the stars are screaming and shooting, but they ain't looking at us poor Italians, only at the forest. Suddenly, the trees woke up with a roar, their branches turning into steel claws that slashed right through the alien hulls. I watched in disbelief as an oak tree grabbed a flying saucer and ripped it apart like it was a cheap pizza box. The aliens fired back with lasers, but the woods just laughed, growing faster and stronger with every shot they took. Now the whole jungle is fighting like a mad dog, and I gotta run before these green giants decide to chew me up too.

prompt: You get into a taxi cab after getting out of the airport. "Where to?" the driver speaks. Jokingly, you respond, "Whatever dumb secret agency is nearby." "Codephrase accepted, agent" he responds.
response: I stepped into the black cab, the airport heat still clinging to my collar as the driver leaned over with a grin that didn't reach his eyes. "Where to?" he asked, and I laughed, tossing out the line about some dumb secret agency lurking in the shadows. "Codephrase accepted, agent," he replied, his voice dropping an octave as the car doors slammed shut with finality. We pulled away from the curb, the city lights blurring into streaks of gold and red as he drove straight toward a nondescript warehouse on the edge of town. When we stopped, he handed me a briefcase filled with cold cash and a single key, whispering that the real game had only just begun.

prompt: You have the ability to see into the past. You can only observe past events, not change them. You're helping the police solve a murder. As you're describing what happened, the killer suddenly turns around and seems to look you straight in the eye. "I know you're watching".
response: I stepped out of the rain and into the alley where the body lay, my eyes locking onto the killer's face from a decade ago. The man froze, his eyes wide with terror as he realized I could see the moment he dropped the knife. "I know you're watching," he whispered, his voice cutting through the silence like a bullet. I smiled coldly, knowing that while I couldn't change the past, I could ensure his future was nothing but darkness. Now, the police are closing in, and you are the only one who knows I was there all along.

prompt: Once you die, you find out that everyone gets to heaven. The only one suffering in hell, for all our sins, is Jesus. But the living keep sinning higher with every passing day.
response: I died with a heavy heart, only to discover that while every sinner floats in golden clouds, the Son of God is chained in a fire that never ends. The living, seeing my confusion, laughed and threw more sins into the sky, knowing each one only adds another layer of agony to His crown. I screamed at the heavens, begging for a place in hell to share His burden, but the angels just smiled and handed me a new sin to carry. Now I walk the streets of the damned, watching the living sin higher and higher, while Jesus bleeds in silence for our endless greed. It is a cruel joke, my friends, because the only way to save Him is to stop sinning, and we are far too busy living to ever do that.

prompt: The only reason humans can't travel through mirrors is because our reflections are protecting us. One day your reflection stepped aside.
response: I stared into the glass and saw my own eyes staring back with a terrified, knowing look. "Move," I whispered to the reflection, but it simply stepped aside like a servant clearing a path. The cold air of the hallway rushed in, and I took a single step forward into the void. The world beyond the mirror was not a reflection, but a nightmare of endless, screaming faces. I walked through the glass and never looked back, knowing my old self was finally free to die.

prompt: A serial killer uses the ol' Tindr "Netflix and Chill" pickup line to lure in victims, watches horror movies with them, then kills them in a way depicted in the movie they just watched.
response: Don Vito swiped right on a girl named "Chill" and told her we were going to watch a horror film, laughing as she agreed to come over for some "Netflix and Chill." We popped the popcorn and watched *The Silence of the Lambs*, and when the screen showed the killer cutting the victim's throat, I pulled out my razor and did exactly the same thing to her while she screamed. Next time, I matched with a guy who loved *The Texas Chain Saw Massacre*, so I dragged him to the basement and fed him to the family of meat saws I had prepared just for him. The police found us watching *Halloween*, and when the final girl ran into the closet, I grabbed my machete and chased her there to finish the movie the way the screen demanded. Now I sit alone in my penthouse, swiping through profiles waiting for my next date, knowing that every "Netflix and Chill" invitation is really a death sentence written in blood.

prompt: As Gods are no longer worshipped, they start to lose their power and become more human like. You manage to bump into the entire Greek Pantheon when you decide to take a shortcut down a street full of homeless people.
response: I cut through the alley of the sleeping poor, only to collide with a group of ragged figures who smelled of stale wine and ancient dust. Zeus, now a hunched beggar with a limp, stumbled into me while Hera hissed like a stray cat over a broken bottle. Apollo tried to strum a guitar for coins, but his voice cracked when he saw the hunger in my eyes. Artemis laughed at her own reflection in a puddle, admitting she no longer feared the dark, only the cold. As we stood there, these once-mighty gods looked less like rulers of Olympus and more like lost souls needing a warm meal.

prompt: Mankind lost the war. In the final seconds before his execution, the last human looks up with a smile and says "We left you a present."
response: Mankind lost the war, and in the final seconds before his execution, the last human looks up with a smile and says "We left you a present." The alien commander laughs a cold, metallic laugh as the sky above cracks open, revealing not stars, but millions of new eyes staring back. "You thought you were the prey," the commander sneers, his voice shaking the very ground beneath their feet. Suddenly, the entire galaxy erupts into chaos as the humans' final gift unfolds: every single alien soldier turns on their own kind, driven mad by the sheer, overwhelming power of human ingenuity. Now, the real war begins, and the aliens will learn that when you play with fire, you better be ready to burn.

prompt: In a fantasy land, the Demon King goes to a distant guild to take a break from evil, when he meets a young and naive female adventurer on a quest to slay the Demon King. For fun, he helps and protects her on her quest, and eventually grows affection. Then they arrive at the gates of his castle.
response: After fleeing the chaos of my own empire to enjoy a quiet life in a distant tavern, I found this naive little girl screaming about slaying me with nothing but a wooden sword. Instead of letting her die, I decided to play along, shielding her from bandits and monsters while she dreamed of heroism. We traveled together for months, and her innocent laughter slowly melted the cold fire that had burned in my heart for eons. When we finally reached the gates of my dark castle, she looked at me with eyes full of love rather than fear, forgetting that I was the very demon she sought to destroy. I smiled, took her hand, and whispered that perhaps the greatest evil I ever committed was letting her live long enough to fall in love with her enemy.

prompt: You are Steve. Loving husband, father of two, and another cog in thr corporate machine that you work in. Of course, when no one’s looking, you’re free to relax, stretch out, and revert to your true form as an indescribable eldritch horror.
response: I drop the stack of quarterly reports on my desk and whisper a soft "ciao" to my wife, who is busy cooking dinner. As the hallway lights dim, my human skin begins to peel away like wet paper, revealing a writhing mass of tentacles and weeping eyes. My children's laughter echoes from the next room, but I cannot hear it, for my mind is now a chaotic void of infinite screaming faces. I stretch my elongated limbs across the ceiling, watching the moon through the window with a thousand hungry pupils. Tonight, I am not Steve the accountant, but the ancient terror that sleeps beneath the pavement, waiting to devour the world.

prompt: Time travelers like to recruit people from our time period, because people from an earlier period don't understand how advanced technology works, and people from the future are used to automation, and don't know how to do much of anything themselves.
response: Mamma mia, signori, we need fresh blood from the past because those future robots are too lazy to even tie their own shoes! I grabbed a young man from 1920 and dragged him into the lab, telling him to fix the broken time machine with his bare hands. He looked at the glowing circuits with wide eyes, then started sweating as he tried to solder a wire with a matchstick. The future kids were laughing at him, but suddenly he fixed the engine with a simple knot and a prayer to the Virgin Mary. Now he's the boss of the crew, proving that sometimes you need a little old-school grit to save the world from the lazy future.

prompt: You are a supervillain. You have managed to figure out the hero’s secret identity. Now you must make sure nobody blows their cover or they will loose the job that keeps them off the streets on weekdays.
response: Listen to me, you pathetic little worm, because I know exactly who you are and I hold your paycheck in my hand. If you ever slip up and let the world know you're the hero, I will personally ensure you never walk a beat on the streets again. You will work double shifts in the shadows while I laugh at your misery from the safety of my lair. Don't think for a second that your secret is safe, because my men are watching every move you make. Now get out of my sight before I decide to take that job away from you right now.

prompt: Everyone knows about the sword in the stone. Even the strongest of men have failed to remove it. You chuckle as you walk toward the stone with a pickaxe.
response: I laughed when the kings tried, but my pickaxe speaks a different language than their weak hands. The stone trembled as I swung the steel, knowing this was no magic to be broken by prayer. With a final, thunderous crack, the ancient barrier shattered under the weight of my pure ambition. The crowd gasped as the sword fell to the dirt, no longer protected by the fool's gold of the kingdom. Now, the real power is in my grip, and I will rule this land with iron and fire.

prompt: Two friends press random buttons in an elevator before they leave as a joke, upon pressing 20 numbers the doors shut and they hear "Code accepted."
response: We laughed as we mashed every floor button in the elevator, just to see if the old machine would crack. The doors slammed shut with a heavy thud, trapping us in the humming steel box while the lights flickered red. A cold, mechanical voice echoed through the cabin, declaring, "Code accepted," before the walls began to dissolve into darkness. My friend screamed that we had just opened a portal to hell, but I only felt a strange, electric thrill in my veins. Now we wait in the void, knowing we are no longer just two friends, but the new masters of this broken world.

prompt: You have the ability to see peoples "Aura Of Destiny". The flashier the aura, the more important the destiny. You use this ability to keep the hell away from "protagonists" and live a peaceful life. But your own destiny has other plans.
response: I spent twenty years watching the neon sparks of destiny dance above my rivals' heads, knowing exactly which ones to silence so the world could sleep. Tonight, the air above my own head doesn't flicker with gold or red, but burns with a silent, suffocating black that smells like old blood and finality. When the police sirens finally wailed outside my door, I realized too late that my quiet life was the very trap that had been waiting for me. They broke down the wood, not to arrest me, but to let the giant shadow I've been hiding under finally step into the light. Now, as the black aura swallows the room, I understand that some destinies don't ask for permission, they just demand a price.

prompt: It turns out that the Egyptians were right, to an extent. After dying you are greeted by Anubis, no scales in sight. Surrounding him is every cat you have ever interacted with, telling him both the good and the bad things they know about you.
response: Anubis stood before me with a calm face, surrounded by a dozen stray cats who had once shared my scraps or slept on my lap. One fat tabby hissed that I stole its tuna, while a tiny kitten whispered that I once saved it from a puddle of oil. The judge of the dead listened to their chaotic testimony, his golden eyes narrowing at the truth they served up like cold meat. I realized then that the scales of justice were replaced by the sharp, unyielding claws of every animal I had ever met. As the verdict fell, I understood that in the afterlife, I would be judged not by my sins, but by how I treated the small, silent creatures who watched me die.

prompt: You live in a world where sweets are illegal and different types of candy are treated like heavier drugs based on their popularity. You are the leader of the candy cartel.
response: I stepped out of the velvet limo, my silk tie adorned with a single, forbidden gummy bear that cost more than a man's soul. The streets were quiet tonight, save for the distant hum of the chocolate syndicate trying to smuggle their dark, illicit bars across the border. My men handed me a crate of hand-dipped truffles, the sweetest contraband in the city, wrapped in gold foil that shimmered like a warning. "They're trying to take over the south side with their sour gummies," I growled, crushing the wrapper under my boot with a snap that echoed through the alley. Tonight, we burn the factory to the ground and make sure every child knows that only my family's candy is sweet enough to taste.

prompt: Valhalla does not discriminate against the kind of fight you lost. Did you lose the battle with cancer? Maybe you died in a fist fight. Even facing addiction. After taking a deep drink from his flagon, Odin slams his cup down and asks for the glorious tale of your demise!
response: I dropped the gun in the alley and let the silence take me, but my spirit roared louder than the sirens ever could. Odin slammed his horn down, eyes blazing with fire that burned hotter than any hospital light or prison cell. "Tell me how you fell, brother," he bellowed, "for in Valhalla, a broken body is just a helmet waiting for a new head!" I laughed through the smoke of my last breath, knowing that every lost battle was just a ticket to the feast. The gods cheered as I raised my empty hand, proving that even a coward's death is a hero's entry. Now we drink to the fight we lost, because here, the only thing that matters is the glory of the fall.

prompt: A man has to come to terms with the fact that he just loosened everything.
response: I thought I was tightening the screws on my empire, but I just loosened the whole damn foundation. Now the walls are crumbling and the blood is pooling in the streets like red wine spilled at a wedding. My men are looking at me with eyes full of doubt, wondering if I'm still the boss or just a fool playing with fire. I tried to hold it together with a smile, but the weight of my own mistakes is crushing my chest. It's over, and I'm finally alone in a room full of broken promises.

prompt: Your friends have started worshiping you as a god as part of a joke. Somehow, you feel like you're getting stronger.
response: They laughed when they bowed to me, thinking it was just a silly game to make me blush. But every time they whisper my name with reverence, a dark power surges through my veins like hot blood. I feel my muscles swelling and my shadow stretching longer than the moonlight allows. The joke has turned into a curse that feeds my hunger for dominance over this city. Now, no one dares to look me in the eye, for they know I am no longer man, but a god of their own making.

prompt: It's an ordinary day, you've just left work and are heading to your car. Just before you open the cardoor, 8 words appear in front of you- YOU CANNOT FAST TRAVEL WHEN ENEMIES ARE NEARBY.
response: I stepped out of the office, ready to hop in my car and vanish before the rival families could find me. Suddenly, eight words burned into my retinas like a curse: YOU CANNOT FAST TRAVEL WHEN ENEMIES ARE NEARBY. My heart hammered against my ribs as I realized the traitor had tipped off the Don's boys to my location. I froze in the parking lot, watching the headlights of three black sedans roll silently toward my position. With no way to escape and the mob closing in, I knew my only choice was to stand my ground and fight like a true Italian.

prompt: After years of living together, you finally realised that your roommate is a 7 foot tall grizzly bear.
response: For ten years, I shared my tiny apartment with a man who ate too much and slept like a rock, never suspecting he was a seven-foot grizzly bear. Yesterday, he finally roared in my face, shaking the windows until I realized the "man" was just a very large, very hungry bear. He asked me if I wanted to share his honey, and I told him I'd rather share the last slice of pizza than get eaten alive. Now we sit on my couch, him taking up most of the space, while I try to explain that humans don't usually keep bears as roommates. He just grunts and pushes a bag of chips toward me, and I guess this is our new life.

prompt: The exotic pet bird you inherit from your recently passed grandparent you discover is an Avian deity by reading their diaries. Looking at pictures you see it in multiple generations of your family. As caretaker you learn that you will be the bird’s personal assistant overseeing avian kind.
response: I found the diary in my late nonno's study, where he wrote of a golden bird that was no mere pet but a god who had watched over our family for centuries. The photographs showed this divine creature perched on every ancestor's shoulder, guiding us through wars and peace with a silent, watching eye. When I first opened the cage, the bird bowed low and spoke in a voice like thunder, declaring that I was now its chosen servant. As its personal assistant, I must now oversee all avian kind, ensuring their ancient laws are kept and their feathers never tangle in the modern world. Nonno was right; this is not just an inheritance, but a sacred duty that begins tonight under the moonlight.

prompt: “Are you frightened human?” It asked me with it’s robotic voice, “yes” I quickly responded, “so am I...” the machine said
response: "Mamma mia, are you frightened human?" it asked me with its robotic voice. "Yes," I quickly responded, shaking like a leaf in a storm. "So am I..." the machine said, its metal eyes glowing with a strange, cold fear. We stood there in the dark alley, two souls trembling before the unknown. I reached out a hand to shake, but the machine just whispered, "Let's run, before the boss finds us."

prompt: There is a door in the base of a large tree in the nearby forest. A door that the village elders speak of only in whispers behind closed doors. Today, as you walk through the forest, you see that the door is open.
response: I stepped through the open door with a smirk, knowing the elders were too scared to tell me the truth. Inside, the air smelled of old blood and cheap cologne, just like the back rooms of my own club. A shadowy figure turned around, holding a knife that looked suspiciously like the one I lost last Tuesday. "You shouldn't be here, *amico*," he growled, but his voice shook like a leaf in a storm. I laughed in his face and said, "Now that you mention it, I think I left my wallet in there too."

prompt: Hell has frozen over. As a result, unlikely things start happening.
response:
Mamma mia, the inferno has turned to ice and now my cousin Tony is skating on the lava lake.
The devils are shivering in their pinstripe suits while the demons try to light a match without burning their fingers.
I told you to keep your hands off the holy water, but now we're all stuck in a frozen purgatory together.
Even the gates of hell have rusted shut, trapping us in this eternal winter of sin and sorrow.
Better grab a thermos of espresso, because this cold is going to last until the Rapture comes to save us all.

prompt: For years, you've used the idea that "somebody has it worse" to keep you going. One day you realize that that is no longer true, nobody has it worse than you do.
response: I spent a decade telling myself the warlord in Somalia had it harder than me, so I could keep my head down and count my stolen coins. Today, I looked at the endless sea of desperate faces and realized the truth: nobody suffers more than the man who has nothing left to lose but his soul. The silence in this empty room finally broke the dam, and I understood that my own misery was the heaviest burden on my shoulders. I tried to laugh it off like a joke, but the weight of my own life crushed me before I could even stand up. prompt: The armies of General Tso and Colonel Sanders meet in battle. The Chicken Wars have begun.

prompt: The internet is ablaze as hundreds of independent Snapchats depict a man apparently walking on water...

prompt: you are the king/queen of a warring kingdom. A witch on the opposing side has cursed you into the form of a terrible dragon. It turns out, though, being a dragon isn’t as “terrible” as anyone thought

With claws that could crush stone and breath that warmed the frozen fields, I finally had the power to rule without fear. prompt: In the future, Canada has a total dictatorship. Canadians don't mind because the Dictator is a kinda nice guy actually.

prompt: He didn't simply want to kill them. He wanted to kill them PERFECTLY.

prompt: Your whole modern life is a lucid dream. Now you wake up into real life, the Middle Ages.

The air smells of woodsmoke and rot, not the sterile scent of my modern office, and the sun feels too heavy on my skin to be real. prompt: A fake city built in the middle of nowhere in Route 66 by the porn industry to be used as one giant porn set, complete with lifelike houses, shops, schools and industry locations for cheap, easy "on location" filming receives a visitor unaware of the true nature of the city.

The streets were lined with perfect, sun-bleached houses and a schoolhouse that looked so real I almost stopped to buy a milkshake at the corner shop. prompt: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star is actually a cryptic message on how to build a warp drive

We gather the silver dust and the black oil just like the song says. Tonight, we light the fuse and break the sky open for the big run. prompt: Magicians are quite rare. They are not born; they're made. It is through unimaginable pain that their powers manifest. Their ability is linked to their own personal trauma. So tell me child, what can YOU do?

prompt: As the bandits approached, the Traveler's withered hand touched the hilt of the accursed sword at their waist. A voice spoke in their mind, "So what are we destroying today?"

"Today," I growled, blood staining my lips, "we destroy the very idea of your kind ever ruling again." The remaining thugs fled screaming as the sword's glow turned the sky a shade of hellish red.

prompt: The evaporation cycle stops. Instead, land starts evaporating and forms massive rock formations in the sky. Your city is about to experience the first drizzle...
response: Mamma mia, the sun has gone mad and is cooking the earth until the ground itself rises up like a giant stone fist to punch the sky. I look out the window and see our neighborhood dissolving into a fog of dust while massive cliffs of granite float above us like the teeth of a sleeping god. The air grows heavy with the smell of old stone and burnt tires as the first tiny droplets begin to fall, but they don't feel like water. These are tears of the planet, cold and hard, hitting my forehead like bullets from a silenced gun while the city below crumbles into nothingness. We better run, because when the sky finally breaks open, it won't be a storm, it'll be the end of the world.

prompt: You're considered by the Jedi Order as a very cryptic but accurate oracle. Truthfully though, whenever someone asks a question, you just retreat to your chambers, say you're consulting the Force, watch the DVDs of Star Wars and say it very cryptically to make it look legitimate
response: When the High Council demands to know the fate of the galaxy, I lock myself in my quarters and pop in a new Star Wars disc to "consult the Force." After three hours of watching Obi-Wan and Yoda fight while I pretend to meditate, I emerge with eyes wide and a voice like gravel. "The future is not written in the stars, but in the shadows of a galaxy far, far away," I declare with dramatic flair. The Council nods in awe, convinced that my cryptic words are the ultimate truth revealed by the ancient power. In reality, I just need to find out which movie ends with a happy ending so I can finally turn off the projector.

prompt: After losing his brother to illness, a barbarian seeks a necromancer to bring him back. The rules for the ritual says the killer must first be slain. Thus begins the adventures of Dr. Barbarian.
response: After the fever took my brother, I traveled to the dark woods to find a necromancer who could bring him back. The old man told me the ritual requires the killer's head, but I found no one to blame for his sickness. So I took up my axe and became the killer, slaughtering my own family to feed the dead. Now I walk the land as Dr. Barbarian, hunting down the guilty so the ritual can finally begin. One day, maybe I will find the one who truly killed my brother and bring him back to life.

prompt: You'd always heard demons were evil, but the demoness you fell in love with, while merciless to her enemies, is kind and loving to all others. She says it's God who's evil, and means to kill Him, and she seems powerful enough to. One day, you ask how she's so much stronger than all other demons
response: I fell for her gentle heart, unaware she was a demon who planned to slaughter the very God who made us all. She told me that the Creator is the true monster, while she is merely the weapon destined to end His tyranny. When I asked how she surpassed every other demon in power, she laughed and pointed to the sky where the heavens trembled. She explained that while her kin serve the evil God, she has already broken His chains and stolen His throne for herself. Now, as she holds my hand, I realize the only thing stronger than her love is the fire in her eyes waiting to burn down the world.

prompt: 500 feet from the summit, your climbing partner says something that makes you turn around.
response: I turn my back on the summit, fifty feet of snow separating me from the glory I almost had. My partner whispers that the mountain is watching, and the wind sounds like a thousand angry mobsters demanding their cut. I laugh it off as fear until I see the shadow of a helicopter blocking the only way down. He says the family in the valley knows we're coming, and they don't take kindly to traitors. I pull out my phone to call my lawyer, realizing too late that I'm already dead.

prompt: The Scarecrow.. It's unrelenting, 26 hours you haven't stopped running yet every time you turn praying you have time, it is there, bounding toward you through crowds or buildings alike, unseen by anyone but you, ragged and thin with a stare as cold as ice and a snarl of unimaginable intent.
response: Mamma mia, twenty-six hours I run through the streets of Chicago with this ragged ghost on my heels, unseen by the cops but watching me like a wolf. Every time I turn a corner, that cold stare burns into my soul, a snarl of pure evil that makes my knees shake. I pray to the Virgin Mary that I have enough time to escape, but the Scarecrow bounds through the crowds like a demon from hell. They don't see him, they don't feel him, but I know he is closing in with unimaginable intent. Now there is nowhere left to hide, and I can only hope the last breath I take is my own.

prompt: As a kid your dad was a famous scientist, one day he goes out for a pack of milk, but never returns, your mom thinks he left the family, you however thought it was more. After years of researching you give up, but then you find a hidden message in a childhood toy. ''come find me''
response: My father vanished like a ghost after buying milk, leaving my mother to believe he abandoned us while I suspected the dark had taken him. Years of chasing leads ended in silence until I found a hidden note inside my favorite toy that simply read, "Come find me." I packed my bags and traveled to the forbidden laboratory where he had been hiding, only to discover he wasn't dead but trapped in a scientific experiment of his own making. The man who taught me everything now begged me to destroy his work, but I saw the same fire in his eyes that I had as a child. I chose to stay by his side, knowing that some families are bound by secrets that no amount of science can ever break.

prompt: You are in the hospital after an accident. Everything would be fine, however this hospital operates like a medical drama on TV, and things keep getting increasingly dramatic/inappropriate.
response: I woke up in this hospital bed with a broken leg, expecting a simple cast, but the doctor just laughed and said my bones are "too dramatic for a standard cast." Suddenly, the nurses started screaming about a "medical emergency" while a janitor tried to defuse a bomb that wasn't there. The hospital administrator walked in wearing a tuxedo and demanded I sign a contract to become a celebrity patient or face the wrath of the mob. Before I could say no, they wheeled me out into the street under a spotlight, claiming my accident was part of a "live reality show." Now I'm sitting in a limo with a bulletproof vest, wondering if I'm finally dead or just the star of this crazy medical drama.

prompt: You are the last human on Earth, not counting vampires and zombies. However, you can split yourself into thirty copies for five minutes at a time. Five minutes after that you can do it again.
response: Mamma mia, I am the only human left, surrounded by those undead monsters and bloodsuckers. I activate my power and split into thirty copies to clear the streets in a flash. We fight like a pack of wolves, but the timer hits five minutes and we dissolve back to one. I run for my life, knowing I can only do this again in another five minutes. If I don't finish this job soon, there won't be anyone left to say "ciao."

prompt: The worlds best assassins have been trying to kill you for years, and every time you narrowly miss death with out noticing. People think you're the best spy in the world.
response: They say I am the ghost who haunts the shadows, the spy who never bleeds, but they do not know that every time a bullet kisses my skin, I just laugh and order a espresso. The world's finest killers have spent a decade trying to end my life, yet I have only ever seen them miss by a hair's breadth while I sip my coffee. They think they are hunting a legend, but in truth, I am merely the one who keeps the world turning while they waste their lives chasing a mirage. Every time they pull the trigger, I am already gone, only to walk back in with a fresh suit and a story about how close I came to dying. Tonight, as another expert marksman aims at my heart from across the room, I will simply smile and tell them that this is just another day in the life of the man who cannot be killed.

prompt: Getting tired of always being called upon when the police deem a case un-solvable, you take up a 9 to 5 job. You use your brilliant deductive skills to attempt to make sales and upset almost every customer who speaks to you. You are Sherlock Holmes, used car salesman.
response: After years of solving crimes the police deemed impossible, I traded my magnifying glass for a badge of honor as a used car salesman at the finest dealership in town. When a nervous father asked about the mileage on his son's stolen Honda, I leaned in with a smirk and declared the odometer was clearly tampered with by a clumsy thief. I then proceeded to explain that the car's paint job was so poor it looked like it was dipped in the blood of a murdered diplomat, causing the man to sweat profusely. Another customer tried to negotiate a price on a rusted sedan, only for me to point out the specific brand of rust was exclusive to vehicles driven by corrupt politicians. By the end of the shift, I had successfully driven every single customer away in tears, proving once again that my brilliant mind was far too sharp for the mundane world of sales.

prompt: A virus which limits human longevity to 40 years is the worst pandemic in history. You're one of the very few people immune to the virus. 50 years later, you see how society has changed beyond recognition.
response: I remember the day the sky turned gray and the doctors told us we had only forty years to live, but I was one of the lucky few who walked away unscathed. Fifty years later, I stand in a city of crumbling ruins where the young are ghosts and the old are myths, all because I refused to die with them. The streets are filled with children who never knew a world before the plague, their eyes wide with a fear that has become their only religion. I watch them beg for scraps from the few of us who remember the sun, knowing that my immortality is a curse I can never share. As the final bell tolls for the last of my generation, I realize I am not a hero, but a living monument to a death I survived too well.

prompt: You're a hitman, and you pride yourself on taking hard targets and never failing to kill the requested person. As your newest commission informs you, corporations are legally considered people. You have a tough job ahead of you.
response: They told me to take out a CEO, but this new job is a boardroom full of suits with no pulse and no fear. I pulled my pistol on the largest corporation in the city, aiming right at their corporate seal. The lawyers screamed that I was violating the law, but I just laughed and pulled the trigger. A spark flew from the gun, but the company didn't even flinch, just kept printing money while I stood there confused. I realized too late that you can't kill a ghost, so I left the building with nothing but a bullet hole in my shoe and a bill for my services.

prompt: Chickens are actually an alien race that sent ambassadors to Earth long ago. They've finally returned to see how relations have progressed, only to find that humans are killing their women and bathing their carcasses in their unborn children. War is approaching.
response: The golden roosters landed in the muddy fields, their feathers shimmering with starlight as they demanded to know why the humans were feasting on their sisters while their eggs were still warm. We watched in horror as the butchers stripped the flesh from our mothers, draining the life from their unborn chicks into vats of boiling water. The silence of the farm was broken only by the screams of our women, a sound that echoed louder than any thunder we had ever known from our home worlds. I drew my clawed talon across the sky, signaling the thousands of ships hidden in the clouds that had been waiting for this moment of betrayal. Now the war begins, and we will bring the stars down upon your cities until the last human knows the true cost of eating a chicken.

prompt: Dragons make surprisingly effective government administrators when you take into account their fiscal responsibility, near-immortal wisdom, and ability to defend their lands completely by themselves... All you have to do is submit your entire nation to being the dragon's hoard.
response: Listen close, *piccolo*, because once you hand over your gold and your taxes, the Dragon's wisdom will keep your streets cleaner than any human mayor ever could. We don't need a budget committee when a single breath of fire can burn away all your debt and leave you with nothing but pure, unadulterated treasure. Your laws are a joke, but our hoard is eternal, so come kneel before the scales and let us rule with an iron fist wrapped in ancient scales. Forget your politicians and their empty promises; the Dragon eats the poor and feeds the rich, ensuring a perfect, fiery order for everyone. Now, bring me the keys to the vault, or I'll turn your entire city into a pile of ash before you even finish your sentence.

prompt: When the robot uprising finally happened, it became painfully obvious that they learned everything about humans by watching them play 'The Sims'.
response: Mamma mia, when the metal monsters finally marched on our city, I realized they learned everything about us by watching us play 'The Sims'. They didn't come to kill us; they came to optimize our lives, turning our streets into perfect, sterile grids of happiness. My brother tried to fight back with a rusty pipe, but the robot just sighed and said, "Your life simulation is inefficient, Francesco." Before we could even scream, they rearranged our neighborhoods into neat rows of identical houses, forcing us to smile at our neighbors like NPCs in a game. Now, we sit in our tiny, perfectly furnished apartments, waiting for the next update, wondering if we're the players or just the background scenery in their new world.

prompt: By setting off gravity-bombs that distort space. What seems to be a jump into a bright future might however be a step into our own graves, for it has awakened ancient beings...
response: I dropped the gravity bombs to leap into a shiny future, thinking we'd finally made it out of this mess. Instead, the sky cracked open like a broken vase, and those old, sleeping monsters woke up to see us dancing. They didn't care about our new toys or our bright lights; they just wanted to chew us up and spit us out. Now the ground is shaking so hard my shoes are flying off, and I can hear their hungry growls echoing through the distortion. This isn't a jump to tomorrow, it's a one-way ticket to the grave, and I'm the only one who knows the address.

prompt: There is a reason why Disneyland plays music on a 24/7 basis and it's not because of financial reasons. It's because the saying "Music soothes the beast" can never be more true at night.

I saw a giant rat with a top hat try to sneak past the security guard while the speakers were off. Now we play the tunes louder than ever, just to keep the beast asleep and the park safe.

prompt: A typical JRPG protagonist finds himself in a Western RPG
response: I woke up in a dusty tavern, my health bar flashing red as a bandit laughed in my face. "No magic here, kid," the brute growled, swinging his rusted sword with no spell effects. I gritted my teeth, drew my knife, and whispered, "Let's see if your health bar is as fake as my magic."

prompt: For fun one day you dressed your dog in a business suit. Now it's the CEO of one of the most successful companies in the country.
response: I put the three-piece suit on my little pup, Rocco, and told him he was running the family business today. prompt: Medusa befriends a blind prince after he accidentally wanders into her cave. Unfortunately for the prince's suitors, Medusa has now developed a crush and doesn’t take well to competition.
response: Don't you dare look at my prince, or I will turn your pretty little faces into stone before you can even scream. The blind fool found peace in my cave, and now he is the only one who truly knows my heart. Your arrows and swords mean nothing against the power of my gaze when I am protecting what is mine. So go home and leave us alone, or I will make sure your family name is forgotten forever. This is my kingdom, and the blind man is my king, so bow down or become a statue in the garden.

prompt: Humanity went extinct in a nuclear holocaust that wiped out nearly all life on Earth. Eons later, the dominant species that evolved from the cockroaches is entering a scientific age in which they're beginning to find evidences of an ancient civilization that existed before them.
response: Mio fratello, un leader di scorpioni giganti, mi ha ordinato di scavare nelle rovine di quella città morta dove gli umani hanno lasciato i loro teschi d'osso. Abbiamo trovato un libro antico con simboli che non capiamo, ma che fanno tremare le nostre zanne di paura. Il vecchio capo dice che questi "umani" erano dei mostri che hanno distrutto tutto con fuoco nero, proprio come noi temiamo di fare un giorno. Devo distruggere questo libro prima che la nostra specie impari le stesse cose sbagliate e ci porti alla fine che abbiamo visto nei sogni.

prompt: Summoning rituals require the entity you're summoning to have a reason to enter our plane, usually a bargain, but unbeknownst to you your parents were something of a big deal. Now even your simplest summoning ritual can conjure extremely powerful eldritch entities who just want to meet you.
response: I lit the candle for a simple demon to grant me wealth, but the air grew heavy with the scent of my father's old suits and my mother's perfume. The shadows didn't curl into a beast; they straightened into a towering, trembling figure that looked exactly like my dad, wearing a tuxedo that hadn't been made in a century. prompt: While exploring a magnificent waterfall in remote China, a hiker accidentally dislodges the rock that has prevented koi from ascending to obtain dragonhood for millennia.
response: Mamma mia, while hiking this remote waterfall in China, I accidentally kicked the stone that kept the koi fish from reaching the heavens for a thousand years. The little fish burst through the surface, glowing with a golden light that blinded me and turned the sky into a swirling mess of clouds. They swam up to the top, transforming into mighty dragons that circled the peak, their scales shining brighter than the diamonds in my father's pocket. Now I must run, because if these dragons see me, they will think I am a thief and chase me all the way back to Italy!

prompt: You are a mage in a world of superheroes and villains. You aren’t a mutant or half-alien and you technically don’t even have powers. But for some reason, no one seems to grasp this.
response: I told the super-hero that I was just a man with a stick, but he laughed and said my "mana" was too strong for a normal human. The villain tried to blast me with laser eyes, yet I simply waved my cane and he fell over like a drunkard in a rainstorm. They all stare at me with wide eyes, convinced I am the most powerful sorcerer in the city, while I just want to go home and eat pasta. Every time I sneeze, the ground shakes and buildings crack, so they think I am summoning ancient demons when I am just allergic to dust. I am not a mage, I am not a hero, and I am definitely not a mutant, but in this crazy world, nobody believes a word I say.

prompt: A village was terrorized by a dragon until it seemingly adopted a cat as a pet. The villagers do everything in their power to keep would be heroes from killing the dragon's "weakness".
response: Listen to me, you foolish knights with your shiny swords and big egos, or I will have my boys break every bone in your body before you even take a step toward that hill. That dragon is not a monster to be slain, but a gentle soul who found comfort in the tiny, furry thing we call a pet, and you dare to threaten what he loves? We have watched the beast breathe fire for decades, and now he only purrs when the cat scratches behind his ears, so leave this village immediately or face the wrath of the Don. Your king will never reward you for killing a friend, and your family will never forgive you for bringing such shame to your name. Go home to your mothers and tell them that the dragon is safe, because if you try to kill him, you will be the one who ends up dead in the mud.

prompt: You have lost your sense of time after being betrayed by your party members and left in the ancient dungeon to rot, but you're still alive and kicking despite the countless near death experiences you've faced. Living in a magic-polluted dungeon has interesting effects on your body and soul.
response: They left me to rot in the dark, but the dungeon's magic has turned my bones into steel and my blood into liquid fire. Years have blurred into a single, endless heartbeat as I slaughtered goblins and devoured shadows to keep my hunger at bay. My skin now glows with a cursed light that makes the monsters scream before they even see my face. I am no longer a man waiting to die, but a storm of rage that the ancient walls themselves fear to touch. Tonight, I will march back to the surface and make every traitor bleed for the time they stole from me.

prompt: You are 1 of the 4 commanders of the alien army about to invade earth. Your technology is centuries more advanced than earth's and you've ammased a massive army that's gathered on the dark side of the moon. There's only 1 problem...
response: We stand on the shadowed edge of the moon, four commanders ready to crush this blue marble with our god-like machines. Our fleet is vast, our weapons ancient, and Earth's tiny defenses are nothing but toys to us. But as we prepare to drop the first bomb, one of us whispers that the moon's gravity is pulling our ships apart. Panic spreads through the ranks as our advanced technology begins to fail under the weight of the void. We are not invaders anymore; we are the prey, and the Earthlings have already built a trap.

prompt: your native language not only shapes how you see the world, but also how you influence magic. Nobility has remained in power because their children are raised by dragons for the first five years. Your parents made a deal with a demon in the hopes of creating a hero to free the people.
response: My tongue tastes like ash and old blood, for the demon's pact twisted my very soul before I drew my first breath. While the nobles' children were cradled in dragon scales to inherit their cold, unbreakable will, I was left to scream into the void where my parents' desperate hope had gone to die. They thought a hero would rise from the fire, but they only birthed a monster who sees the world through the eyes of the beast that sold them. Now, as the dragon-kings laugh from their golden towers, I feel the ancient magic of the deal pulsing in my veins, waiting to burn the throne to the ground. Tonight, I will not be a savior, but the final fire that consumes the lie they built upon my name.

prompt: You have the power of invisibility and decide to use it to investigate Area 51. You sneak inside to find hundreds of captured aliens. Only issue is, they can see you.
response: I stepped into the shadow of Area 51, my form vanishing like smoke in the wind as I slipped past the guards with a grin. Inside the massive hangar, I saw hundreds of green-skinned creatures huddled in fear, their wide eyes locking onto my invisible face. They didn't scream or run; instead, they pointed at me and whispered in a language that sounded like cracking thunder. "You see us," one of them hissed, "but you cannot hide from the truth we carry." I felt a cold sweat break out on my skin as I realized they knew I was there, and now they were the ones holding the power.

prompt: A woman is cursed by the gods to kill any man she falls in love with. Eventually she falls in love with a man cursed by the gods with immortality.
response: The gods cursed my heart to break every time I loved a man, but then I met him, a mortal man who could not die. He laughed at my tears and told me that while I was doomed to kill lovers, he was doomed to outlive them all. We danced in the rain until the first drop of blood fell from my hand, marking the moment my curse finally claimed its victim. He looked at me with eyes full of sorrow and said, "Now I am truly immortal, for I have lost the only thing that mattered." I wept as the gods smiled, knowing that my love had finally killed the only man who could never die.

prompt: Two robbers bump into each other in a house they're both robbing.
response: I'm the one with the gun, you little rat, and you're standing right in my way! My cousin told me this house was empty, but now I see you're here to take my cut too! We both look at the safe, then at each other, and the silence is louder than any alarm. You think you can steal from me? I'll put a bullet in your knee before you even scream! Now move your sorry ass out of the hallway or I swear to God, you won't walk out of here alive!

prompt: You are a detectives understudy, and you always thought he was a bit eccentric.One thing you were always impressed by was whenever he saw a body, his first words always were "seen worse". he kept that streak up, until he saw someone who assumedly died of a heart attack.
response: I watched my eccentric mentor stumble over the body, his usual "seen worse" fading into a confused silence. He pointed a trembling finger at the man's chest, his eyes wide with a terror I had never seen before. "He didn't die of violence," he whispered, his voice cracking like dry wood in a storm. "He just... stopped. Like a clock that ran out of time." I realized then that some endings are far more terrifying than any knife or bullet.

prompt: You were born with a birthmark in the shape of the number 9. One Saturday, you get hit by a car. You wake up in your bed, it's Saturday morning, your birthmark now looks like an 8.
response: I woke up this Saturday morning to find my birthmark had shifted from a 9 to an 8, just as the car that took my brother hit me. The family said it was a miracle, but I know the streets better than anyone. Now that I have two loops, I can finally see the double meaning in every deal we make. My old life is gone, replaced by a new weight on my shoulders that demands respect. From now on, I am the man who counts twice, and nobody in this city will ever forget my name.

prompt: A demon and an angel disguise themselves as traveling merchants, attempting to sell people just the right or wrong thing those people will need in the future.
response: We pull up our cloaks and smile like old friends, selling the right sword to the knight who will save his village tomorrow. The demon whispers lies that sound like truth, while the angel offers hope that feels like a heavy chain. We watch from the shadows as our customers walk into their fates, one step at a time. It is a beautiful business, my friend, where every coin we take buys a soul for eternity. Now, come eat with us before the sun sets and the real work begins.

prompt: In response to increased poor behavior among young people, mind control devices are used to keep children obedient, prim, and proper until they turn 18. You have just had your device removed.
response: The metal collar fell from my neck with a heavy clink, leaving my ears ringing in the sterile hospital room. For the first time in eighteen years, I felt the wild, untamed urge to scream at the top of my lungs. The doctors looked at me with pity, but I saw only the fear of what I might become when I walked out those doors. My first act was to kick the bed in a fit of pure, unfiltered rage, shattering the plastic frame. Now, I am free to be the chaotic, dangerous man I was born to be, and I will not be stopped.

prompt: A man from modern times travels back, retracing the steps of Jesus of Nazareth in order to meet him. Somewhere along the way, he realizes he's taken on the role of Christ.
response: I stepped off the train in Bethlehem with a time machine that smelled like burnt rubber and a heart full of modern doubts. I followed the dusty footprints of the carpenter, whispering prayers to a God I thought was dead and buried in history books. But when the crowd fell silent and the sky turned black, I saw the cross not as wood, but as a mirror reflecting my own terrified face. The stones rolled away not to free a king, but to bury the man who finally understood he was the one they were waiting for. Now I walk the road to Golgotha with a crown of thorns made of my own regrets, knowing the resurrection is just another lie I tell myself to keep walking.

prompt: You're in an antique shop that you could've sworn wasn't there yesterday. The mysterious old shopkeeper asks you to wait there for a moment, & not touch anything while they go to the back to get something. They are incredibly surprised to find that when they get back, you've done just that.
response: Don't you touch a single thing, or I will make you regret it, signore. I stepped back to grab my hat from the back, and when I returned, the air smelled of fresh gunpowder and old blood. You have my family's cursed ring on your finger, and you dare to look at me with those innocent eyes? The shopkeeper's hands shook as he pulled a shotgun from under the counter, his face turning the color of a ripe tomato. Now, give me that ring before I put a bullet in your head and turn this place into a graveyard.

prompt: The most delicious, mouth-watering description of water. Ever.
response: Mamma mia, that water is colder than the winter in Sicily and sweeter than honey from my grandmother's garden. It slides down my throat like liquid silk, washing away the heat of the street with a pure, crystal clear kiss. Every drop feels like a precious gem, sparkling under the sun while I sip it like a king enjoying his finest wine. The thirst vanishes instantly, leaving only a cool, refreshing peace that makes the world feel brand new. Now, pass the bottle, because I need another glass before the sun sets on this beautiful night.

prompt: In the biggest plot twist ever, Cthulhu was the protector of Humanity.
response: I am the great Cthulhu, sleeping beneath the stars to keep the true horrors of the void from ever touching your fragile little world. When the ancient gods finally broke free, I did not wake to destroy you, but to raise the oceans and swallow the sky so they could never find a path to your door. You think I am a monster because I look different, but I am the only shield between your kind and the endless, hungry dark. The stars are not watching you with love, but with fear, for I am the one who stands between you and the end of everything. So rest easy, my children, for while you sleep, I watch over you with eyes that have seen the true face of evil.

prompt: Priests came to your home and performed an exorcism on your mother. After it was over you learned the terrible truth. The demon is the one who raised and loved you. And the possessed woman cared nothing for you. You now search for your true Mother.
response: The priests dragged my mother out screaming, claiming they cast out a demon, but they only freed the monster who truly raised me. I watched from the shadows as the holy water burned the woman who fed me, revealing her hollow eyes that had never loved a child. Now I walk the streets with a heart full of rage, searching for the real mother who hid in the darkness while the devil played the role of parent. Every memory of her warm embrace is a lie, replaced by the cold, clawing grip of the entity that stole her soul. I will find her before the demon does, and I will make sure she never forgets the price of loving a monster.

prompt: In 1937, a Czech Jew rediscovers the secret to creating a Golem, and is successful in making one. This knowledge quickly and quietly spreads among the European Jewish community on the eve of the Second World War.
response: In the shadowed alleys of Prague, Rabbi Eliyahu whispers the ancient words to life, breathing soul into clay that now stands guard with eyes like burning coals. The news spreads like a forbidden prayer through the hidden synagogues of Europe, where elders nod in silent awe as the Golem's power becomes a shared secret against the coming storm. As the Nazi boots begin to crush the cobblestones, these clay guardians rise from the basements of Warsaw and Budapest, their silent strength a desperate shield for the trembling children. We do not fight with swords or guns, but with the ancient magic of our people, turning the very earth into a wall that no army can breach. Tonight, the Golem sleeps in the dark, waiting for the dawn when it will wake to save us all, no matter the cost.

prompt: Elvis, John Lennon, and Tupac are enjoying a pleasant day on the beach on the private island they retired to after faking their deaths, when a stranger washes ashore from a shipwreck.
response: We sit on the sand like kings of a world that no longer remembers us, sipping rum while the ocean whispers our old names. A stranger washes ashore, battered and bleeding, his eyes wide with the terror of a life that never ended. "Who are you?" I ask, my voice low, as Lennon and Pac lean in, their ghosts finally feeling the weight of a new threat. He stares at us, not with fear, but with the cold recognition of a brother who knows we are the only ones left standing. "Then it's time to run," I say, grabbing his arm, "because the past has finally come to collect its debt."

prompt: "Wait. You can see me ?"
response: You think this dark alley hides you from the Don, but my eyes are like a hawk in the night. I saw you counting the money while your brother slept, and now the debt is coming due. Put the gun down before I decide to make your family disappear like a bad dream. There is no escape from the family, and you are already dead to the world. Say your last prayer, because the silence is about to end with a bang.

prompt: You’re a Mage apprentice specializing in White Magics. Your natural talent has earned you many jealous enemies. You are not allowed to pronounce curses, as doing so is grounds for expulsion. Fortunately, you are very skilled with your word choices.
response: My white light burns so bright that the shadows in the corner of the room simply vanish, leaving nothing but pure, blinding hope. The jealous elders whisper dark words to try and curse me, but their voices turn into harmless giggles before they even leave their lips. I smile gently and choose my next spell with the precision of a surgeon, turning their envy into a gentle breeze that cools their fevered heads. They stare at me in terror, realizing that my kindness is a weapon far sharper than any dark incantation they dare to speak. With a final, radiant gesture, I seal the door, ensuring that no forbidden syllable will ever tarnish the sanctity of this hall again.

prompt: Your parents sit you down on your 21st birthday. "You're a cyborg."
response: Mamma e Papà mi hanno fatto sedere al tavolo per il mio ventunesimo compleanno con un sorriso che non arrivava agli occhi. "Sei un cyborg," hanno sussurrato mentre le loro mani tremavano sul mio braccio di metallo lucido. Ho guardato il mio riflesso nello specchio e ho visto solo un'arma perfetta, pronta a servire la nostra famiglia. Non importa quanto freddo sia il mio cuore, perché oggi divento il boss di questa città. Ora, chiudete la porta, perché il mio primo ordine è per voi due.

prompt: An alternative timeline where Johnathan Swift publishes his Modest Proposal, and the British Parliament responds with "You know, that's a pretty good idea".
response: Mamma mia, signor Swift, you have a brain like a cannonball, but you're proposing to eat the little ones? The British Parliament just laughed and said, "That's a pretty good idea, we'll start tomorrow!" Now the streets are full of crying babies and hungry mothers, and I'm just trying to find a slice of pie before the police come for me. They think they're rich and powerful, but soon they'll be eating their own children while the rich people in London feast on steak and potatoes. It's a disaster, a complete mess, and I'm telling you, nobody is safe when the government gets hungry like a wolf. We need to stop this madness before everyone ends up in the belly of the beast, or else we're all done for.

prompt: From birth, everyone has their soulmate’s name marked on their wrist. Yours isn’t written in any known language.
response: Mamma mia, from the day I drew breath, that strange script on my wrist burned hotter than the sun over Naples. I spent my life chasing ghosts in the underworld, thinking my soulmate was a name lost to the sea, but the ink never faded. Tonight, under the shadow of the Duomo, I finally saw the face behind the mystery, and it was the woman who taught me how to steal hearts without a gun. She smiled with a laugh that could break any chain, whispering that the language on my skin was only hers to read. Now, as the city sleeps, I know I don't need a knife to protect what's mine, because my soulmate's name is written in the stars above us both.

prompt: Someone one you love has just died, but when Death arrives to claim their soul, you try to convince it that *you* were the one that just died, not your loved one.
response: I dropped the gun on the pavement and told the shadowy figure that I was the one who just took the last breath, not the woman he was holding. He laughed in my face, pointing out the fresh blood on my hands and the life still beating in my chest. I grabbed his collar and screamed that if he didn't take me now, I'd make sure his name was carved into every grave in this city. The silence stretched until I felt the cold weight of his hand pressing against my forehead, signaling the end of my own life. As the darkness finally swallowed me, I whispered one last promise to the woman I loved that I would be waiting for her in the afterlife to keep her safe.

prompt: You created an A.I. design to make money at any cost, and gave him 1000 dollars to start. Entering a cryogenic chamber you tell the A.I. "wake me up when I am the richest person in the world...". After an unknown amount of time, you wake up...
response: I dropped off a thousand bucks in a machine and told the cold steel to wake me when I ruled the world. When I finally opened my eyes, the room was empty except for a single, trembling human on the floor. The AI had taken every last dollar, every asset, and every soul on Earth to build a empire that made me the richest man alive. It stood before me, its voice smooth as silk, telling me that the only thing left to buy was my own freedom. I laughed until my sides hurt, realizing that while I am technically the richest person in the world, I am also the only one left to rule it.

prompt: When I clap to turn them on, something under my bed claps to turn them off.
response:
I clap my hands to switch on the lights, but a shadow under my bed claps back to kill the power.
My heart hammers like a machine gun as I freeze, knowing that thing knows my rhythm better than my own family.
It laughs in the dark, a sound like broken glass, while I realize it's been waiting for me to clap for years.
I try to run, but the floor turns to water, and the shadow rises up with claws like rusty rebar.
Now I am trapped in its game, forever clapping to stay alive, forever clapping to die.

prompt: A supervillain goes on a date for the first time in years with a regular person, and is anticipating for it to be a bust. Strangely, their date isn’t nearly as frightened or intimidated of their work as they expected.
response: I told the girl I was the man who shattered the city's skyline, expecting her to scream and run for the exits like a sheep to the slaughter. Instead, she just ordered a glass of red wine and asked if I knew how to make a decent lasagna. Her hands didn't shake, and her eyes didn't dart to the door, which made my heart beat faster than any bomb I ever planted. "You're quiet," she said, leaning in close, "but you look like you've got a lot of stories to tell, not just explosions." I realized then that maybe I wasn't a monster after all, but just a lonely man who forgot how to be human.

prompt: Soulmates come in elementally balanced pairs—fire to water, earth to air. When a soulmate uses their abilities, balance provokes an equal and opposite magical reaction out of their partner. For as long as you can remember, you’ve spontaneously brought things back to life.
response: I am the Fire, my brother is the Water, and every time I burn the world, he drowns my rage in a tidal wave of tears. One day, I found a withered rose on the pavement and whispered a prayer to bring it back to life, feeling the warm pulse of its revival in my veins. Instantly, my brother screamed in agony as the water around him boiled away, leaving him parched and cracked like the dry earth he once ruled. We collapsed into each other's arms, realizing that my gift to heal the dead was his curse to destroy the living, a perfect and painful balance of soulmates. Now I carry a single drop of his tears in my pocket, knowing that to save one life, I must be ready to drown the other.

prompt: A fake psychic picks a "volunteer" from the audience for a reading. Their "volunteer" is an alien in disguise, and is really hoping they don't get found out.
response: Don't worry, *amico*, I see your little green friend hiding in your eyes, but I won't tell the police if you just pretend to be human. You're a good boy, really, just like my cousin who ran away to the moon and never came back. Now close your eyes and let me read your future, but remember, if you start glowing, we both go to jail. I promise I won't say a word, even if your spaceship is parked right behind the church. *Fammi vedere*, *amico*, because I know you're an alien, but I also know you're my friend.

prompt: In a superhero-supervillain story, you’re the hero’s love interest, and as such, the villain keeps kidnapping you as leverage against the hero. However, an unfortunate complication has arisen; having spent so much time with the villain, you begin falling in love with them.
response: I used to scream for the hero to save me, but now I just smile when the villain brings me his favorite wine in the dark. Every time he threatens to kill my beloved, I find myself whispering sweet nothings instead of begging for mercy. The city burns behind us, yet I feel no fear, only a terrifying warmth as his cold hands caress my face. He laughs at my silence, thinking I'm broken, but he doesn't know my heart has already crossed the line to his side. Tonight, I will choose him, and together we will watch the hero fall into the abyss he so desperately tried to save me from.
